body:
# Release Notes - v1.19.2 ## Fixes ### Split expenses no longer show $0 reimbursable when one line is personal When an employee split a card charge into a business line and a personal line, the expense list showed **$0 reimbursable** for the whole expense and the business part was left out of the next reimbursement run. The reimbursable amount now reflects the business lines only, and affected expenses from the last 30 days have been recalculated and added to the next run. ### Mileage claims over 100 miles never triggered the second approver Policies that require a second approver for long trips compared the distance in kilometres against a limit set in miles, so claims between 100 and 160 miles skipped the second approval. Distances are now compared in the unit the policy was written in. ### Overview showed $0 pending when the only pending items were advances The Overview tile counted pending expenses but not pending cash advances, so a team with only advances outstanding showed **$0 pending**. Advances are now included and labelled separately in the tile tooltip. --- ## Enhancements ### Clear reimbursement dates for expenses approved after the cutoff Expenses approved after the payroll cutoff used to say "Reimbursement scheduled" with no date. They now show the actual pay date of the next run, and the employee notification includes the same date. ### Wider duplicate detection coverage - cross-card matches and hotel folio splits Duplicate detection now also compares charges across an employee's different cards and recognizes a hotel folio that was submitted both as one expense and as nightly lines. These matches are **advisory**: they add a warning for the approver but never block submission or approval. --- ## Technical details
Split-line reimbursable calculation - personal lines excluded at the ledger - The reimbursable amount is computed from line items flagged `business` instead of from the expense header, in both the list query and the reimbursement run builder. - A one-off job recalculated split expenses submitted in the last 30 days and queued the difference for the next run.
Unit-aware distance thresholds for approval chains - Policy thresholds now store their unit; the approval chain converts the claim distance into the policy's unit before comparing. - Existing policies were migrated with the unit of the company's home country.
Overview pending total includes advances - The pending tile sums expenses and cash advances in one query; the tooltip lists them separately.
Reimbursement date resolution - The next pay date is resolved from the payroll calendar at approval time and stored on the expense, so later calendar edits do not change dates already shown to employees.
Cross-card and folio duplicate matching - New matchers compare amount, merchant, and date across all cards owned by the same employee, and match a folio total against the sum of nightly lines within one stay. - Results are advisory only: they attach a warning to the approval view and are never used to block an action.
Test-only - split-line invariant - New property test asserts that the reimbursable amount never exceeds the sum of business lines for any split expense.
Scope, build, and deploy - `main...development` ships **#1012, #1031, #1046, #1055, #1058**. #1012 and #1031 are merged but stay dark until v1.20.0 enables them. - No new env vars. One migration: `20260901090000_add_unit_to_policy_thresholds`, additive with a default. - Deploy order: ledger service first, then the web app; no downtime required.
